Lab 3. Understanding Data Quality¶

In this lab, you will get hands-on experience with preparing a dataset for a regression task.

Specifically, we will go through the following steps:

  • Load the Palmer Penguins dataset.
  • Inspect columns, data types, summary statistics, and feature relationships.
  • Find missing values and compare beginner-friendly repair strategies.
  • Identify possible outliers with the IQR rule.
  • Winsorize numeric data with scipy.
  • Prepare a clean regression dataset and split it into train and test sets.
  • Save the cleaned files for later modeling work.

The regression task is to predict body_mass_g using the other columns as features.

Step 3A. Required Plot: Flipper and Bill Length¶

This recreates the required plot from the prompt:

  • flipper_length_mm on the x-axis
  • bill_length_mm on the y-axis
  • one marker/color per species
  • one simple regression trend line per species

The trend lines are calculated with basic pandas arithmetic.

In [8]:
X_PLOT = "flipper_length_mm"
Y_PLOT = "bill_length_mm"
GROUP_COL = "species"

required_plot_columns = [X_PLOT, Y_PLOT, GROUP_COL]
missing_plot_columns = [col for col in required_plot_columns if col not in df.columns]

if missing_plot_columns:
    raise ValueError(f"Missing required plot columns: {missing_plot_columns}")


def add_pandas_regression_line(ax, group_df, x_col, y_col, color):
    """Add a simple least-squares line using pandas Series arithmetic."""
    x = group_df[x_col]
    y = group_df[y_col]

    denominator = ((x - x.mean()) ** 2).sum()
    if denominator == 0:
        return

    slope = ((x - x.mean()) * (y - y.mean())).sum() / denominator
    intercept = y.mean() - slope * x.mean()

    x_line = pd.Series([x.min(), x.max()])
    y_line = intercept + slope * x_line
    ax.plot(x_line, y_line, color=color, linewidth=3)


def plot_flipper_and_bill(
    data,
    subtitle="Dimensions for Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo Penguins at Palmer Station LTER",
    save_path=None,
):
    """Create the flipper/bill scatter plot with per-species trend lines."""
    plot_df = data.dropna(subset=required_plot_columns).copy()

    species_styles = {
        "Adelie": {"color": "#ff7f0e", "marker": "o"},
        "Chinstrap": {"color": "#8a2be2", "marker": "^"},
        "Gentoo": {"color": "#008080", "marker": "s"},
    }

    fallback_styles = [
        {"color": "#1f77b4", "marker": "D"},
        {"color": "#2ca02c", "marker": "P"},
        {"color": "#d62728", "marker": "X"},
    ]

    species_order = [species for species in species_styles if species in set(plot_df[GROUP_COL])]
    extra_species = [species for species in sorted(plot_df[GROUP_COL].unique()) if species not in species_order]
    species_order.extend(extra_species)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 7))

    for i, species in enumerate(species_order):
        group_df = plot_df[plot_df[GROUP_COL] == species]
        style = species_styles.get(species, fallback_styles[i % len(fallback_styles)])

        ax.scatter(
            group_df[X_PLOT],
            group_df[Y_PLOT],
            label=species,
            color=style["color"],
            marker=style["marker"],
            s=55,
            alpha=0.85,
            edgecolors="none",
        )
        add_pandas_regression_line(ax, group_df, X_PLOT, Y_PLOT, style["color"])

    fig.suptitle("Flipper and bill length", x=0.075, y=0.98, ha="left", fontsize=18)
    ax.set_title(subtitle, loc="left", fontsize=13, pad=10)

    ax.set_xlabel("Flipper length (mm)", fontsize=12)
    ax.set_ylabel("Bill length (mm)", fontsize=12)

    ax.set_xlim(168, 232)
    ax.set_ylim(30, 62)
    ax.set_xticks([170, 180, 190, 200, 210, 220, 230])
    ax.set_yticks([30, 40, 50, 60])

    ax.grid(True, which="major", color="#e0e0e0", linewidth=1)
    ax.minorticks_on()
    ax.grid(True, which="minor", color="#eeeeee", linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)

    ax.legend(title="Penguin species", frameon=False, loc="lower right")

    plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95])

    if save_path is not None:
        fig.savefig(save_path, dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight")

    plt.show()
    return fig, ax


fig, ax = plot_flipper_and_bill(df, save_path="flipper_bill_plot.png")

Step 5. Fix Missing Data: Options¶

Two common beginner-friendly choices are shown below.

Option 1: remove rows with missing data.
Option 2: fill missing numeric values with mean values. Categorical columns do not have means, so this notebook fills categorical missing values with the most common value, also called the mode.

For regression, rows with a missing target value are usually removed. Do not invent target labels unless your instructor specifically asks you to.

Step 6. Choose a Missing-Data Strategy¶

Set MISSING_DATA_STRATEGY to either "drop" or "fill".

This cell always removes rows where the target is missing. Then it either drops remaining rows with missing feature values or fills missing feature values.

In [16]:
MISSING_DATA_STRATEGY = "fill"  # Choose "drop" or "fill".


def fix_missing_for_regression(input_df, target_col, strategy="fill"):
    """Return a dataframe with missing data fixed for a regression task."""
    output_df = input_df.copy()

    # For supervised learning, rows with missing target values are not useful for training/evaluation.
    output_df = output_df.dropna(subset=[target_col]).copy()

    if strategy == "drop":
        output_df = output_df.dropna().copy()

    elif strategy == "fill":
        numeric_feature_cols = [
            col for col in output_df.select_dtypes(include="number").columns
            if col != target_col
        ]
        categorical_feature_cols = [
            col for col in output_df.columns
            if col not in numeric_feature_cols and col != target_col
        ]

        for col in numeric_feature_cols:
            output_df[col] = output_df[col].fillna(output_df[col].mean())

        for col in categorical_feature_cols:
            if output_df[col].isna().any():
                modes = output_df[col].mode(dropna=True)
                fill_value = modes.iloc[0] if not modes.empty else "Unknown"
                output_df[col] = output_df[col].fillna(fill_value)

    else:
        raise ValueError("strategy must be either 'drop' or 'fill'")

    return output_df.reset_index(drop=True)


df_missing_fixed = fix_missing_for_regression(df, TARGET, MISSING_DATA_STRATEGY)

Step 7. Identify Outliers¶

This notebook uses the IQR rule to flag possible outliers.

For each numeric column:

Q1 = 25th percentile, Q3 = 75th percentile, IQR = Q3 - Q1

The lower bound is Q1 - 1.5 * IQR, and the upper bound is Q3 + 1.5 * IQR.

Values outside those bounds are flagged as possible outliers. A flagged value is not automatically wrong; it means you should inspect it.

In [17]:
numeric_columns_fixed = df_missing_fixed.select_dtypes(include="number").columns.tolist()

q1 = df_missing_fixed[numeric_columns_fixed].quantile(0.25)
q3 = df_missing_fixed[numeric_columns_fixed].quantile(0.75)
iqr = q3 - q1

outlier_bounds = pd.DataFrame({
    "q1": q1,
    "q3": q3,
    "iqr": iqr,
    "lower_bound": q1 - 1.5 * iqr,
    "upper_bound": q3 + 1.5 * iqr,
})

outlier_bounds.round(2)

Step 8. Winsorize Numeric Data with Scipy¶

Winsorization caps extreme values instead of deleting rows.

With 5% lower and 5% upper limits, the smallest 5% of values are capped at the 5th percentile and the largest 5% are capped at the 95th percentile.

By default, this notebook winsorizes numeric features and leaves the target column unchanged. Set WINSORIZE_TARGET = True if your instructor wants the target column winsorized too.

In [21]:
WINSOR_LIMITS = (0.05, 0.05)
WINSORIZE_TARGET = False

if WINSORIZE_TARGET:
    winsor_columns = numeric_columns_fixed
else:
    winsor_columns = [col for col in numeric_columns_fixed if col != TARGET]


def winsorize_series(series, limits=(0.05, 0.05)):
    """Winsorize one pandas Series while preserving the original index."""
    nonmissing = series.dropna()

    if nonmissing.empty:
        return series

    capped_values = winsorize(nonmissing, limits=limits)

    result = series.copy()
    result.loc[nonmissing.index] = pd.Series(list(capped_values), index=nonmissing.index)
    return result


df_winsorized = df_missing_fixed.copy()

for col in winsor_columns:
    df_winsorized[col] = winsorize_series(df_winsorized[col], limits=WINSOR_LIMITS)

comparison = pd.DataFrame({
    "before_min": df_missing_fixed[winsor_columns].min(),
    "after_min": df_winsorized[winsor_columns].min(),
    "before_max": df_missing_fixed[winsor_columns].max(),
    "after_max": df_winsorized[winsor_columns].max(),
    "before_mean": df_missing_fixed[winsor_columns].mean(),
    "after_mean": df_winsorized[winsor_columns].mean(),
}).round(2)

print("Winsorized columns:", winsor_columns)

Step 10. Split into Training and Test Data¶

This uses pandas only.

Training set: 80% of rows.
Test set: 20% of rows.

The test set is kept separate so a future model can be evaluated on data it did not train on.

In [25]:
TRAIN_FRACTION = 0.80

train_df = df_model.sample(frac=TRAIN_FRACTION, random_state=RANDOM_STATE)
test_df = df_model.drop(index=train_df.index)

X_train_raw = train_df.drop(columns=[TARGET])
X_test_raw = test_df.drop(columns=[TARGET])
y_train = train_df[TARGET]
y_test = test_df[TARGET]

# One-hot encode categorical variables.
X_train = pd.get_dummies(X_train_raw, drop_first=True)
X_test = pd.get_dummies(X_test_raw, drop_first=True)

# Make sure train and test have the same feature columns after one-hot encoding.
X_test = X_test.reindex(columns=X_train.columns, fill_value=0)

print("Training rows:", len(train_df))

Lab 3. Understanding Data Quality¶

Student version: This copy keeps the setup and helper code in place, but removes a small number of essential solution pieces. Each marked cell has comments and hints showing exactly what to complete.

In this lab, you will get hands-on experience with preparing a dataset for a regression task.

Specifically, we will go through the following steps:

  • Load the Palmer Penguins dataset.
  • Inspect columns, data types, summary statistics, and feature relationships.
  • Find missing values and compare beginner-friendly repair strategies.
  • Identify possible outliers with the IQR rule.
  • Winsorize numeric data with scipy.
  • Prepare a clean regression dataset and split it into train and test sets.
  • Save the cleaned files for later modeling work.

The regression task is to predict body_mass_g using the other columns as features.

Step 3A. Required Plot: Flipper and Bill Length¶

This recreates the required plot from the prompt:

  • flipper_length_mm on the x-axis
  • bill_length_mm on the y-axis
  • one marker/color per species
  • one simple regression trend line per species

The trend lines are calculated with basic pandas arithmetic.

In [ ]:
X_PLOT = "flipper_length_mm"
Y_PLOT = "bill_length_mm"
GROUP_COL = "species"

required_plot_columns = [X_PLOT, Y_PLOT, GROUP_COL]
missing_plot_columns = [col for col in required_plot_columns if col not in df.columns]

if missing_plot_columns:
    raise ValueError(f"Missing required plot columns: {missing_plot_columns}")


def add_pandas_regression_line(ax, group_df, x_col, y_col, color):
    """Add a simple least-squares line using pandas Series arithmetic."""
    x = group_df[x_col]
    y = group_df[y_col]

    denominator = ((x - x.mean()) ** 2).sum()
    if denominator == 0:
        return

    slope = ((x - x.mean()) * (y - y.mean())).sum() / denominator
    intercept = y.mean() - slope * x.mean()

    x_line = pd.Series([x.min(), x.max()])
    y_line = intercept + slope * x_line
    ax.plot(x_line, y_line, color=color, linewidth=3)


def plot_flipper_and_bill(
    data,
    subtitle="Dimensions for Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo Penguins at Palmer Station LTER",
    save_path=None,
):
    """Create the flipper/bill scatter plot with per-species trend lines."""
    plot_df = data.dropna(subset=required_plot_columns).copy()

    species_styles = {
        "Adelie": {"color": "#ff7f0e", "marker": "o"},
        "Chinstrap": {"color": "#8a2be2", "marker": "^"},
        "Gentoo": {"color": "#008080", "marker": "s"},
    }

    fallback_styles = [
        {"color": "#1f77b4", "marker": "D"},
        {"color": "#2ca02c", "marker": "P"},
        {"color": "#d62728", "marker": "X"},
    ]

    species_order = [species for species in species_styles if species in set(plot_df[GROUP_COL])]
    extra_species = [species for species in sorted(plot_df[GROUP_COL].unique()) if species not in species_order]
    species_order.extend(extra_species)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 7))

    for i, species in enumerate(species_order):
        group_df = plot_df[plot_df[GROUP_COL] == species]
        style = species_styles.get(species, fallback_styles[i % len(fallback_styles)])

        ax.scatter(
            group_df[X_PLOT],
            group_df[Y_PLOT],
            label=species,
            color=style["color"],
            marker=style["marker"],
            s=55,
            alpha=0.85,
            edgecolors="none",
        )
        add_pandas_regression_line(ax, group_df, X_PLOT, Y_PLOT, style["color"])

    fig.suptitle("Flipper and bill length", x=0.075, y=0.98, ha="left", fontsize=18)
    ax.set_title(subtitle, loc="left", fontsize=13, pad=10)

    ax.set_xlabel("Flipper length (mm)", fontsize=12)
    ax.set_ylabel("Bill length (mm)", fontsize=12)

    ax.set_xlim(168, 232)
    ax.set_ylim(30, 62)
    ax.set_xticks([170, 180, 190, 200, 210, 220, 230])
    ax.set_yticks([30, 40, 50, 60])

    ax.grid(True, which="major", color="#e0e0e0", linewidth=1)
    ax.minorticks_on()
    ax.grid(True, which="minor", color="#eeeeee", linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)

    ax.legend(title="Penguin species", frameon=False, loc="lower right")

    plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95])

    if save_path is not None:
        fig.savefig(save_path, dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight")

    plt.show()
    return fig, ax


fig, ax = plot_flipper_and_bill(df, save_path="flipper_bill_plot.png")

Step 5. Fix Missing Data: Options¶

Two common beginner-friendly choices are shown below.

Option 1: remove rows with missing data.
Option 2: fill missing numeric values with mean values. Categorical columns do not have means, so this notebook fills categorical missing values with the most common value, also called the mode.

For regression, rows with a missing target value are usually removed. Do not invent target labels unless your instructor specifically asks you to.

Step 7. Identify Outliers¶

This notebook uses the IQR rule to flag possible outliers.

For each numeric column:

Q1 = 25th percentile, Q3 = 75th percentile, IQR = Q3 - Q1

The lower bound is Q1 - 1.5 * IQR, and the upper bound is Q3 + 1.5 * IQR.

Values outside those bounds are flagged as possible outliers. A flagged value is not automatically wrong; it means you should inspect it.

Step 8. Winsorize Numeric Data with Scipy¶

Winsorization caps extreme values instead of deleting rows.

With 5% lower and 5% upper limits, the smallest 5% of values are capped at the 5th percentile and the largest 5% are capped at the 95th percentile.

By default, this notebook winsorizes numeric features and leaves the target column unchanged. Set WINSORIZE_TARGET = True if your instructor wants the target column winsorized too.

Step 10. Split into Training and Test Data¶

This uses pandas only.

The test set is kept separate so a future model can be evaluated on data it did not train on.

X_test = pd.get_dummies(X_test_raw, drop_first=True)
